summary: Five findings remain: two high-severity paths can reverse or misdescribe income in the spoken plan, two lifecycle issues can merge call records or leak Daily rooms during retries and setup failures, and one result-string path hides a state transition that changes payment timing.

findings.title: Estimated income is falsely described as excluded from the plan
findings.evidence: `item_line` applies the same wording to every non-confirmed certainty: `if getattr(item, "certainty", None) and item.certainty != "confirmed": parts.append(f"{item.certainty}, not counted as money until it arrives")`. This includes `Certainty.ESTIMATED`, but `_income_events` counts estimated income in full and only excludes `Certainty.UNCERTAIN`. Consequently, `show_month` can say that an estimated salary is not counted while its cashflow and low point include it.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish estimated from uncertain wording so the result states that an estimate is counted and only uncertain income is described as excluded. Add a `tests/agent/test_plain.py` case that builds a month with estimated income and verifies the item line agrees with `plan.summary.total_in`; retain a companion uncertain-income assertion that it is explicitly left out.

findings.title: Substring-first filing can turn incoming money into an expense
findings.evidence: `_kind_of` evaluates the item before the model-supplied kind and returns on `if any(word in text for word in words)`. Thus an item such as `rent from my tenant` matches the essential word `rent` and returns `ESSENTIAL` before considering `kind="money coming in"`; similarly, `salary advance loan` matches income before debt. This reverses cashflow direction and bypasses the model's language judgment even though the item phrase is not unambiguous.
findings.recommendation: Restrict item-name overrides to genuinely unambiguous matches and allow the explicit kind to settle contextual or conflicting phrases, without adding semantic judgment machinery to the domain. Add coercion tests for `_kind_of("rent from my tenant", "money coming in")` and `_kind_of("salary advance loan", "loan or card")`, then verify through the plain tool that the former increases income rather than outflow.

findings.title: Second-resolution session IDs merge rapid sequential calls
findings.evidence: The identifier is only `stamp = dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")` followed by `sessions.reserve(f"{body.phone}-{stamp}")`. The single-slot registry prevents overlap but not a delete/retry within the same second. The database insert uses `ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING`, so the second call reuses the first row and later updates its verdict, trace, and recording path under the same ID; the in-process verdict map is also keyed by that ID.
findings.recommendation: Make every call ID unique while retaining the phone and sortable timestamp, for example with sub-second entropy or a suffix. Update `tests/api/test_routes.py` to freeze the clock, start/delete/start two calls in one second, assert distinct IDs, and add a store-level test proving both session-history rows remain addressable.

findings.title: Clearing a dated field is omitted from the tool result
findings.evidence: `_change_lines` discards every transition whose new representation is empty via `if not new: continue`. Dating an income back from a range clears `latest_date`, and changing a dated essential to spread clears `due_date`; the domain reports changes such as `("5 Oct", "")`, but the model never receives that removal even though it changes when money moves. This contradicts the HLD contract that moved values return old beside new.
findings.recommendation: Represent cleared fields explicitly in the result rather than skipping them. Add a `tests/agent/test_plain.py` tool test that first dates an essential, then marks it spread, and asserts the result communicates both the new spread state and removal of the old due date; add the equivalent range-to-single-date case for income.

findings.title: A token-creation failure leaves the newly created Daily room behind
findings.evidence: Setup performs `room_url, room_name = await create_room(settings)` and then creates two tokens inside one `try`, while the `except Exception` path only executes `sessions.release(session_id)` before re-raising. If either token request fails, no session task exists to run `run_session` teardown, so the private room remains until expiry despite the lifecycle requirement to delete rooms after calls or failed setup.
findings.recommendation: Best-effort delete a room that was successfully created when subsequent setup fails, while still releasing the reservation and preserving the original error. Add an API test where `create_room` succeeds and the first or second `create_token` raises, asserting the slot is freed and `delete_room` is called exactly once with the created room.
